sub_theme: Biogas, anaerobic digestion and municipal-waste-to-energy (incl. incentive effects)
methods: Study types: review 3; other 2; techno-economic-assessment 2; empirical-case-study 1. Aspen Plus or cost-based TEA in R0446; literature reviews in R0154, R0206, R0286; Techno-economic models with IRR/NPV/LCOE (R0495); multi-criteria ranking (R0051).
settings: Sectors: agriculture 4; multi-sector 3; buildings-residential 1. Departments: Santander 1; Antioquia 1; Córdoba 1; Atlántico 1; 4 studies national or unspecified.
technical: BMP 0.03-0.78 Nm3 CH4/kg VS [R0154]; AcoD raised yield 14-22% [R0154]; average biogas 2.6 m3/d, 0.21 m3 biogas/kg biomass [R0218]; Theoretical biogas potential 149,436 TJ/year and technical potential 53,554 TJ/year [R0286]; 996 digesters, 79% tubular psychrophilic [R0154]; only about 30% of large-scale biogas used [R0154]; HCCI engine net indicated efficiency about 32%, intake temperature above 320 C [R0435]; Energy potential 1,001-3,283 MWh/day [R0495]; TOPSIS ranking: anaerobic digestion 78.2%, gasification 47.5%, incineration 27.4%, landfill gas 6.6% [R0051]
economic: 7 m3 biodigester yields about US$400/year fuel savings [R0206]; Polyethylene digesters cheapest: 18.2 M USD for 150,718 households [R0446]; LPG saving USD 30/month [R0218]; incineration NPV 396-412 million USD [R0495]; landfill gate fee 7.8 USD/t [R0495]
environmental: biogas cuts firewood GHG to 11% [R0446]; avoiding 0.52 t CO2eq/month [R0218]; low-cost digesters cut impacts up to 80% [R0154]; GHG 46-92% below landfilling [R0495]; GHG mitigated weighted 16.17% [R0051]
pattern: Biogas studies report outcomes on different bases (BMP 0.03-0.78 Nm3 CH4/kg VS and AcoD yield gains of 14-22% in R0154; 0.21 m3 biogas/kg biomass in R0218; theoretical biogas potential 149,436 TJ/year versus technical potential 53,554 TJ/year in R0286). Household digester economics are favourable (about US$400/year fuel savings in R0206; LPG saving USD 30/month in R0218) and GHG reductions are reported in R0446, R0218, R0154 and R0495 (46-92% below landfilling in R0495). For waste-to-energy, R0051 ranks anaerobic digestion first by TOPSIS (78.2%) ahead of gasification, incineration and landfill gas, while R0495 reports incineration NPV of 396-412 million USD.

sub_theme: Biomass resource potential, bioenergy systems, scenarios, policy and sustainability frameworks
methods: Study types: modelling-simulation 3; other 2; review 1; empirical-case-study 1. Residue-to-product-ratio inventories with energy equations (R0323, R0338); Scenario or energy-system models (LEAP in R0152, R0520; TIMES in R0374); sustainability indicator model (R0094); reviews and legal analysis (R0114).
settings: Sectors: multi-sector 6; agriculture 1. Departments: Santander 1; Norte de Santander 1; 6 studies national or unspecified.
technical: Silos highest TEP (up to 208 TJ/yr) [R0323]; source choice changed TEP by up to 30% [R0323]; Residues total 185.66 million t/yr [R0338]; bagasse gives 99.12% of biomass electricity [R0338]; Biomass supplies 315-760 PJ/y of modern bio-based products by 2050 [R0374]; fossil share falls from 76% to 35-39% [R0374]; theoretical bioenergy potential 550,000 TJ vs technical 35,000 TJ (6%) [R0114]; biofuel imports up to 76% [R0152, R0520]
economic: Mobilising biomass cuts system cost by up to 11 billion USD/y and marginal abatement cost by 62% [R0374]
environmental: bioenergy scenarios cut 11.4, 20.3, 22.6, 24.4 MtCO2-eq by 2030 (5-11%) [R0152]; cuts 2030 GHG emissions by 11.4-22.6 MtCO2-eq (5-10% vs baseline 223 MtCO2-eq) [R0520]; BECCS gives 24-29% of cumulative avoided emissions [R0374]
pattern: Potential estimates depend on method and scope: theoretical bioenergy potential 550,000 TJ versus technical 35,000 TJ (6%) in R0114; residues total 185.66 million t/yr with bagasse giving 99.12% of biomass electricity in R0338; source choice changed TEP by up to 30% in R0323. Scenario models (LEAP in R0152 and R0520; TIMES in R0374) all find that bioenergy lowers emissions (11.4-22.6 MtCO2-eq by 2030 in R0520, similar in R0152; BECCS gives 24-29% of cumulative avoided emissions in R0374) but use different baselines; R0094 is a sustainability indicator model.

methods: Study types: modelling-simulation 3; review 1; empirical-case-study 1. LCA (R0012, R0211, R0519); supply-chain optimisation (R0185); reviews (R0272).
settings: Sectors: industry 2; transport 1; agriculture 1; multi-sector 1. Departments: Cesar 1; Atlántico 1; La Guajira 1; Meta 1; Bolívar 1; Cauca 1; 1 studies national or unspecified.
technical: Energy balance -1809 (CS), 90 (CS+AD), -82 (DS), 637 TJ/yr (DS+AD) [R0211]; 12 biodiesel plants, 7 bioethanol plants [R0272]; microalgae need at least 52% less land than oil palm and 67% less than sugarcane [R0185]
environmental: GWP ranged from -287.37 g CO2-eq/FU to 10.219 [R0012]; 8 of 11 cases net negative via land use change [R0012]; GHG 5.3, 0.4, 1.4, -0.3 kgCO2eq/L EtOH [R0211]; GHG 149 (VLT), 93 (ST1), 105 (ST2) kg CO2 eq/t starch [R0519]; biogas cut VLT emissions 72% [R0519]; <5.3% of microalgal areas overlap rainforest vs 30.5-32.4% for oil palm and sugarcane [R0185]
pattern: Evidence is dominated by life-cycle assessment, and GWP varies strongly with feedstock and land-use change (-287.37 g CO2-eq/FU to 10.219 in R0012, with 8 of 11 cases net negative via land use change; GHG 5.3, 0.4, 1.4 and -0.3 kgCO2eq/L EtOH in R0211; GHG 149, 93 and 105 kg CO2 eq/t starch in R0519). Functional units differ, so values are not directly comparable; R0185 adds land-use evidence for microalgae, R0272 an inventory of plants, and no economic outcomes are reported.
